newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais issue another arrest warrant for Khashoggi.
newsitem.headline: Thais issue another arrest warrant for Khashoggi.

text.p: Thai police said on Wednesday they had issued another arrest warrant for Saudi Arabian tycoon Adnan Khashoggi on a separate charge of conspiring to defraud the ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce.

Major General Seri Themeeyavej, chief investigator of economic crimes, told reporters that Khashoggi was wanted for conspiring with five other suspects to defraud the bank of 260 million baht ($10 million).
Earlier this month police issued an arrest warrant for Khashoggi, whose whereabouts are unknown, on a charge of jointly conspiring with five others to obtain two billion baht in loans from the bank.
"Mr. Khashoggi was involved in two cases. So we have to issue a separate arrest warrant today, " another police investigator said.

Among the five charged with Khashoggi in the new case and for whom fresh arrest warrants were also issued on Wednesday were the bank's former adviser Rakesh Saxena and its former president Krirkkiat Jalichandra.
Warrants were also issued for them in connection with the first case against Khashoggi.

The Saudi tycoon was quoted on March 20 by the London-based Arab-language Asharq al-Awsat newspaper as saying that he would take legal action against Thai authorities if they did not drop charges against him.
Thai police said then that he should come to Thailand and try to disprove the charges.

Bangkok Bank of Commerce, saddled with bad loans of more than 70 billion baht, was taken over by the government last year after opposition party charges about the debts triggered a run on its deposits.
